scope: Cars, light trucks and medium/heavy trucks
interpretation: Replace current class weights with the actual legacy weights while holding current class prices, vintage, powertrain, RPE and currency fixed. The table measures this effect rather than assigning the entire gap to fleet weights. For MDVs this changes GVWR shares while retaining current available vocations; legacy Class 3 also included Box, absent from the current ATB price classes.

Legacy CostInvest!AL49:AR54 weights Classes 3 and 7 with AB154:AB155, the same regional/longhaul shipment shares used for heavy trucks. Current school classes receive equal weights. Reusing the legacy weights materially raises the current aggregate and explains why school buses can depart further than source-price and currency differences alone. The supplied database reproduces this formula.

status: Confirmed legacy wiring and current proxy
scope: Medium-truck incumbent powertrains and missing gasoline/CNG prices
interpretation: Legacy gasoline L39 references the CI aggregate AM34; diesel L40 references the SI aggregate AM35. SI additionally omits Class 7 and renormalizes Classes 2–6. Current missing gasoline/CNG prices use the reviewed diesel proxy. Therefore fuel labels alone do not establish equivalent source vehicles. The native-basis residual includes these source-assignment differences.

driver: Dollar year, exchange rate and deflation
interpretation: The legacy worksheet labels its prices 2023 USD and uses its stored USD2023-to-CAD2020 factor; current ATB prices declare 2022 USD and use the selected CER conversion. Their ratio is isolated in the table. Native source amounts also use different dollar years, so their residual cannot be called a pure technology-price change. Raw LDV totals explicitly say 2023$; the MHDV year is inherited from the embedded legacy annotation.

scope: PHEV35 and PHEV50, particularly later vintages
interpretation: The preserved workbook selects Par PHEV35/50, despite the old preparation notebook's intended EREV selection. Current ATB uses extended-range variants. Compare parallel and EREV manufacturing costs in the same raw ANL class, year and Low/Base case before comparing ATB with that EREV value. This separates architecture from weights and the remaining source-price basis.

status: Confirmed source-input changes; full contribution unresolved
scope: LDV FCEVs and MHDV hydrogen technologies
interpretation: FCEV class prices differ before aggregation, with a stronger early-year gap. The ATB archive supplies different fuel-cell/storage cost coefficients, and official assumptions document production-volume adjustments. The component table exposes those inputs. It does not claim a complete full-vehicle reconstruction: sizes and dollar bases must also align, and the old LDV fuel-cell header says 2020$ while its description/vehicle total says 2023$.
evidence: https://atb.nlr.gov/transportation/2024/fuel_cell_electric_vehicle_assumptions; registered ATB ZIP input/inputs_vehicles.csv; raw ANL LDV columns R, CL, CM, CR

interpretation: ATB Mid corresponds to Base performance/Low progress apart from documented fuel-cell adjustments. The review shows each actual purchase-evidence year. Legacy 2040/2045 prices interpolate 2035–2050; the raw LDV reconstruction checks the same interpolation. A prospective five-year shift is not assumed here; a changed timing selection must be assessed from the recorded years.

driver: Units, vehicle scale and SQLite rounding
interpretation: Both calculations convert cost per vehicle to million CAD per thousand vehicles by dividing by 1000. The workbook and raw LDV reconstructions reproduce the supplied SQLite to its nine-decimal storage rounding. These effects cannot explain percentage-scale differences.
evidence: src/parameterization/build_costs.py; legacy CostInvest!L3 and equivalent rows; legacy compile_transport.py parameter rounding

driver: FCEV range inferred from technology names
interpretation: The raw legacy source has one FCEV variant and cycle-dependent ranges; the normalized current ATB FCEV rows do not provide a comparable range series. A 400-versus-300-mile mismatch is therefore unproven. Do not infer it from the backend technology identifier or assign the residual to battery range.
evidence: raw ANL LDV range columns M:N; inputs/1_interim/fetched_nlr_atb_autonomie/atb_vehicles.csv

scope: Motorcycles, intercity buses and representative-archetype scenarios
interpretation: Motorcycles and intercity buses use GCAM/REGEN purchase sources and do not receive the ATB RPE reversal. The current new_capacity_shares mode adds constraints without averaging new-vehicle CAPEX across range variants. Those mechanisms must be checked separately if the source or representation selection changes; the current attribution table covers matched ATB-backed rows.
